summary: PhotoCraft is a free image editor, like Adobe Photoshop. You put photos, colours, shapes and text on separate layers, like a stack of clear sheets. You can edit each layer at any time. With a saved list of steps, PhotoCraft can make the same design again automatically.
use_cases: Make a banner for your blog, newsletter or video channel. Each word, shape and photo stays editable.
Give a folder of holiday or product photos the same size, colours and caption strip in 1 step.
Make all the sizes you need from 1 design: a wide header, a square post and a small thumbnail.
Open and save Photoshop (.psd) files. Share your work with people who use Adobe tools.
story: PhotoCraft made the header picture and the social images of Signal & Noise 2026. The main header shows the key result: Agentic coding grew from 9% to 20% of the conversation. PhotoCraft also made 3 more sizes of the header, such as the square version. It also gave 4 sample photos the same teal and amber colours and a dark caption strip. The page shows 2 of these social cards. A short animation adds more and more noise to the header and then removes it.
recipe: photocraft-cli batch --actions social-card.json --in photos --out cards --format jpg
recipe_note: Make a layered design from a list of steps. Save a Photoshop copy. Apply 1 saved list of steps to a folder of photos.

assets.caption: The Signal & Noise 2026 header shows that Agentic coding grew from 9% to 20% of the conversation.
assets.how: photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":1600,"height":900,"background":"#1B1F3B"}' + 64 --cmd steps (file.placeEmbedded, filter.blur.gaussianBlur, layer.setProps, gradient.fill.create, shape.create, type.create, layer.layerStyle.dropShadow) --out header.pcraft; photocraft-cli convert header.pcraft header.png (args generated by _work/photocraft/make_header.py)
assets.description: PhotoCraft built this header from a list of 64 steps. The layers are a blurred sunset photo, colour gradients, chart bars, a wave line and text with a shadow.

assets.caption: This JPEG copy of the header is a smaller file.
assets.description: PhotoCraft saved the same header as a JPEG file. The file is smaller and loads faster on the web.

assets.caption: Download the editable PhotoCraft file, with more than 60 layers.
assets.description: This is the working file of the header. Each word, bar and shape is on a separate layer. You can change the text or the numbers later.

assets.caption: Download the layered Photoshop file of the header, in a ZIP file.
assets.how: photocraft-cli convert header.pcraft header.psd (zipped with Python zipfile; 4.3 MB unzipped)
assets.description: PhotoCraft saved the layered design in Photoshop format. Adobe tools open it with all layers. The ZIP file makes the download smaller.

assets.caption: The start image is a computer-generated lake scene.
assets.how: Exported by LightCraft, not PhotoCraft: lightcraft-cli run --demo library.select ids=[1] app.export path=.../lake.jpg longEdge=1600
assets.description: LightCraft exported this computer-made landscape from its sample library. PhotoCraft did not change this file.

assets.caption: After the edit, the same scene has the 4 study colours: dark blue, violet, coral and cream.
assets.how: photocraft-cli run src/lake.jpg --cmd image.adjustments.gradientMap --params '{"stops":[[0,"#1B1F3B"],[0.35,"#7A5CFA"],[0.7,"#FF6B4A"],[1,"#F7F4EE"]],"dither":true}' --cmd filter.noise.addNoise --params '{"amount":6,"monochromatic":true}' --cmd filter.sharpen.unsharpMask --params '{"amount":60,"radius":1.2}' --out after_duotone.jpg
assets.description: PhotoCraft changed the dark, middle and light tones of the photo to the 4 study colours. Then it added fine grain and made the edges sharper. PhotoCraft ran all 3 steps in 1 command.

assets.caption: The square version for Instagram shows the main result as text.
assets.how: photocraft-cli batch --actions actions_square.json --in batch_in_header --out batch_out_square --format jpg (image.imageSize, image.canvasSize, shape.create, type.create)
assets.description: A saved list of steps made the header smaller and added dark bands to make a square. It also added the label 'NEW STUDY' and the main result.

assets.caption: The 1200 × 675 version is for posts and link previews.
assets.how: photocraft-cli batch --actions actions_x_post.json --in batch_in_header --out batch_out_x_post --format jpg
assets.description: A saved list of steps changed the header size to 1200 × 675 pixels. It also made the edges a little sharper.

assets.caption: The 640 × 360 thumbnail is a small copy of the header.
assets.how: photocraft-cli batch --actions actions_thumb.json --in batch_in_header --out batch_out_thumb --format jpg
assets.description: A saved list of steps made a small thumbnail from the header. It used the same resize and sharpen steps.

assets.caption: PhotoCraft made this social card of an aurora over hills from 1 saved list of steps.

assets.caption: The header gets more and more noise, then becomes clear again.
assets.how: Frames by PhotoCraft: photocraft-cli run header.png --cmd image.imageSize --cmd filter.noise.addNoise --params '{"amount":N,...}' for N=0...80; stitched into a looping GIF with Python/PIL
assets.description: PhotoCraft made 7 copies of the header, each with more noise. A short Python script joined the copies into this animation.

headless_notes: All steps ran through photocraft-cli run, convert and batch. No window opened. The .pcraft and .psd files keep all layers. PNG and JPG files have 1 flat layer. Text size is in points. Set the resolution to 72 ppi before you add text to high-ppi photos. The CLI has no animation export, so PIL joined the frames into the GIF.
